title: CF Meet calling common definitions v1
description: Canonical, provider-independent call-domain vocabulary shared by the Calling HTTP API, the call-control bodies, the realtime signals and the call lifecycle event contract (Part C sections 15-25). Definitions only: the root schema places no constraints. Provider, SIP, carrier or RTC states are never canonical and must be mapped onto these values by the adapters that observe them.

CallState.description: Canonical business state of a Call. Terminal: ENDED, DECLINED, BUSY, NO_ANSWER, FAILED, CANCELLED.

CallKind.description: Neutral media kind of a Call. No consumer business meaning.

CallFailureCategory.description: Normalized failure category. Provider error codes never become categories.

CallTerminalReason.description: How a Call reached its terminal state. ENDED records its completion evidence; every other terminal state has the reason of the same name.

CallEventType.description: Facts the call domain records. CALL_REQUESTED and CALL_STATE_CHANGED are lifecycle events (they carry states); the others are facts about the Call's children: participants, sessions, routes, legs, attempts, quality, usage, ring offers (invitations), transfers and the Call's media resource. Media facts never carry provider identifiers. Part F: VOICEMAIL_RECEIVED (a mailbox took the Call), VOICEMAIL_READY (the message is stored in protected object storage) and VOICEMAIL_DELETED (its object was removed) carry only opaque ids, a bounded reason and a duration, never an object key, URL or audio.

CallInvitationPurpose.description: Why a ring offer exists: the Call itself, or an application transfer to a new target.

CallInvitationStatus.description: State of a ring offer to one endpoint. PENDING and RINGING are live; every other state is terminal and final (an offer is never revived). The server owns expiry.

CallMediaAccess.description: A session's media authority: NONE until the server authorizes it (initiator, or the single winning device of a participant), AUTHORIZED while it may hold media credentials, REVOKED for ever after removal or the end of the session.

CallTransferState.description: Application transfer lifecycle, kept out of the Call state (the Call is TRANSFERRING while a transfer is active).

CallTransferFailureReason.description: Why a transfer did not complete. A failed transfer returns the Call to its pre-transfer state when the remaining parties still have a media path.

CallEndpointKind.description: Neutral kind of a registered application endpoint (a device / client instance of a principal).

CallEndpointPresence.description: Presence hint used to order ringing; never an authorization.

CallMediaCapabilities.description: Media capabilities the server authorizes for one session's media connection. Derived from server state (call kind, participant permissions, hold); never chosen by the client. There is no administrative, recording, room-creation or room-listing capability.

CallCore.description: Fields of every Call representation (HTTP API, call-control results). Provider-independent: no provider or carrier identifiers, execution bindings, media identities, telephone numbers or protected contact data.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version: 1 at creation, +1 per state transition.

endedAt.description: When the call reached a terminal state.

CallSummary.description: A call as listed and as returned by call-control commands.

SafeText.description: Bounded text without control characters that never looks like a telephone number (+<digit>) or a tel: / sip: URI.

SafeEventData.description: Bounded, flat, privacy-safe event data: at most 32 snake_case keys that never name secrets, credentials, contact data or provider / carrier identifiers; values are booleans, numbers, safe text or short lists of safe text.
